Q: How can I call GitHub Copilot Chat from my Visual Studio Code extension? A:

If you want to send a custom prompt to Copilot chat, you should use the workbench command from the extension:

const prompt = `write two sums with test cases in JavaScript `
vscode.commands.executeCommand('workbench.action.chat.open', prompt);

Q: Error: Function ARRAY_ROW parameter 2 has mismatched row size. Expected: 1. Actual: 10434 A:

try like this with HSTACK:

=QUERY(HSTACK(
 IMPORTRANGE("sheet_name", "Social media posts!A:AI"), 
 IMPORTRANGE("sheet_name", "Social media posts!AJ:AS")),
 "select Col1,Col43,Col23,Col16,Col12,Col44,Col45,Col2,Col3 
  where Col2='instagram'", 1)

Q: Function ARRAY_ROW parameter 2 has mismatched row size A:

as mentioned alreaddy the issue was born but one of your IMPORTRANGE not importing stuff - this throwed you array error. nowadays we can use HSTACK:

=INDEX(QUERY(HSTACK(
 IMPORTRANGE(Links!C2, "Supply!A2:L"),
 IMPORTRANGE(Links!C2, "Supply!A2:B")&
 IMPORTRANGE(Links!C2, "Supply!C2:D")&
 IMPORTRANGE(Links!C2, "Supply!D2:E")),
 "select Col1,Col2,Col3,Col4,Col6,Col7,Col11,Col10,Col9,Col8,Col12
  where lower(Col13) contains '"&LOWER(B1)&"'", ))

but you are still calling same IMPORTRANGE 4x. next time try like this:

=QUERY(LET(i, IMPORTRANGE(Links!C2, "Supply!A2:L"), 
 j, ARRAYFORMULA(OFFSET(i,,,,2)&OFFSET(i,,2,,2)&OFFSET(i,,3,,2)), HSTACK(i, j)), 
 "select Col1,Col2,Col3,Col4,Col6,Col7,Col11,Col10,Col9,Col8,Col12
  where lower(Col13) contains '"&LOWER(B1)&"'", )

Q: Removing characters from std::{w}string A:

temp = temp.substr( 1, temp.length() - 1 ); - as mentioned in the comments, it gets substring on 1 char shorter, but you want to remove 2 characters, so the proper code: temp = temp.substr( 1, temp.length() - 2 );.

This constructs a new string and is not optimal for long strings. A better inplace solution:

temp.erase(0, 1);  // or temp.erase(temp.begin())
temp.pop_back();

Q: How to generate a PDF out of a rendered HTML element? A:

The most cost efficient way to do this at scale is spin off your own node service with headless chrome. In some of my projects what I found easier (if I don't have huge scale) is simply use a service for HTML->PDF like https://agent-gen.com if you have less than 50 pdf generations a month it's even free. There are a few other services that do the same

Q: How do I build libraries in subdirectories using CMake? A:

You are only missing a simple thing: add_subdirectory. From the documentation:

add_subdirectory(source_dir [binary_dir] [EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL])

Add a subdirectory to the build. The source_dir specifies the directory in which the source CMakeLists.txt and code files are located. If it is a relative path, it will be evaluated with respect to the current directory (the typical usage), but it may also be an absolute path. The binary_dir specifies the directory in which to place the output files. If it is a relative path it will be evaluated with respect to the current output directory, but it may also be an absolute path.

add_subdirectory

It does exactly what you need.
